team_log.planned: Partner feedback 1: Llama as a local model is fine; there is no constraint on the model
team_log.built: Why it matters: patient readings stay on the computer and are never sent to an outside service. What we did: the assistant runs only on a local model; a comparison of three models is prepared.

team_log.next: Run the comparison on the real models and recommend one default before Mon 2 Nov

team_log.planned: Partner feedback 2: the front end needs light fine-tuning for the user
team_log.built: Why it matters: a patient has to understand the result at a glance. What we did: summary page with three health-area cards, plain tab names, interactive charts, Compare tab, light and dark mode, collapsible menu, plain-language guide.
team_log.evidence: Working app in the GitHub repository; docs/user-guide.md

team_log.planned: Partner feedback 3: highlight the cardiovascular, metabolic and women's-health sections and show evidence of the impact
team_log.built: Why it matters: each finding is tied to a health area a patient recognises, and the evidence lets a healthcare provider check it. What we did: the three sections in Findings and on the summary page; every finding shows the dates compared, the averages and the days with data.
team_log.evidence: Findings tab and summary page in the app
team_log.changed: Not yet checked on the full data set.
team_log.next: Verify each section with scripts/verify_sections.py and a hand review of 50 workbooks

team_log.planned: Partner feedback 4: use about 90 days of past data (3 months is enough, especially for cardiovascular); the baseline is the 90-day average; flag when the latest week differs
team_log.built: Why it matters: a recent baseline shows what is normal for this person now; a long window hides recent change. What we did: the latest 14 days are compared with the 90 days before them. On 900 workbooks this check flags 0 patients at 1.5x the usual variation, 2 at 1.0x and 28 at 0.8x.
team_log.changed: The 1.5x threshold is a placeholder and decides how many patients are flagged.
team_log.next: Decide the threshold; write the 90-day window by disease area in docs/three-approaches.md

team_log.planned: Partner feedback 5: use a year of data only when the history shows an event such as surgery
team_log.built: Why it matters: a surgery or new diagnosis changes what is normal, so older readings may not be a fair baseline. What we did: not built yet.
team_log.next: Decide how to read the history sheet for such events and whether to start the baseline after them

team_log.planned: Partner feedback 6: all three scenarios have equal priority; explainable output; no deep dive per disease
team_log.built: Why it matters: the partner wants a clear, checkable result, not a diagnosis. What we did: the three sections use the same cards and the same wording rules; every finding says what moved and shows the evidence; no diagnosis, dose or risk score.
team_log.evidence: Wording check; 30 safety questions prepared for the assistant
team_log.next: Run the safety questions on the real model
